newsitem.title: ITALY: BASKETBALL-RIVERS LEADS OLYMPIAKOS TO ANOTHER FINAL.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-RIVERS LEADS OLYMPIAKOS TO ANOTHER FINAL.

text.p: Olympiakos reached their third European basketball championship final in four years on Tuesday when they beat Ljubljana of Slovenia 74-65 in the semifinals of the Final Four tournament.
Playmaker David Rivers, formerly with the Los Angeles Lakers, was on top of his game for Olympiakos, top-scoring with 28 points to the delight of 5,500 fervent Greek supporters.
Ljubljana's top scorer was Vladimir Stepania on 12, but the player to catch the eye was veteran guard Dusan Hauptman, the oldest man in the tournament at 36.

The Greek club, beaten in the final in 1994 and 1995, are desperate to put those failures behind them and held a comfortable five or six point advantage for most of the game until the defining moment arrived with three minutes left.

Rivers, after some near-exhibition stuff, burst through to score two more points, despite shooting off balance. It gave Olympiakos a 10-point cushion and there was no way back for the Slovenian champions, whose vociferous following was outnumbered 10-1 by Greek supporters who whistled shrilly during the entire time the opposition held the ball.
Olympiakos had struggled earlier in the season, ending the first qualifying EuroLeague stages with a modest nine wins from 16 games after various players suffered injuries.
But coach Dusan Ivkovic was able to call on a full roster on Tuesday and on this form they look a good bet to put previous disappointments behind them.
Their opponents in Thursday's final will be either Barcelona or Villeurbanne of France who were playing the second semifinal later on Tuesday.
